What does the guide's example say?","fact_ids":["sec13-F04","sec13-F06","sec13-R01"]},"answer":{"text":"The example says speeding may bring two or three points depending on whether the court was municipal, county or state.","fact_ids":["sec13-F04","sec13-R01"]},"rationale":{"text":"The state law list shows three points, but the example ties speeding points to the court level.","fact_ids":["sec13-R01","sec13-F06"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec13-u01-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"How points reach your record","fact_ids":["sec13-F01","sec13-F02","sec13-F03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Driving is a privilege you can lose.","fact_ids":["sec13-F01","sec13-F02","sec13-F03"]},{"text":"Convictions for moving violations add points.","fact_ids":["sec13-F01","sec13-F02","sec13-F03"]},{"text":"Too many points cost the privilege.","fact_ids":["sec13-F01","sec13-F02","sec13-F03"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson opens the Missouri point system. The guide starts from a simple idea: driving is a privilege rather than a right, and you can lose it by breaking the traffic laws. Points are the tool that tracks those violations. When you are convicted of a traffic violation that happened while your vehicle was moving, the Department is notified and adds points to your driving record. Collect too many points and you can lose your driving privilege. In this lesson we will see how points arrive on your record, and then look at speeding, where the guide gives two different ways of describing the points a conviction brings.","fact_ids":["sec13-F01","sec13-F02","sec13-F03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec13-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Convictions bring the points","fact_ids":["sec13-F02","sec13-R14","sec13-F03"]},"lines":[{"text":"A moving violation leads to a conviction.","fact_ids":["sec13-F02","sec13-R14","sec13-F03"]},{"text":"The Department is notified of the conviction.","fact_ids":["sec13-F02","sec13-R14","sec13-F03"]},{"text":"The Department adds points to your record.","fact_ids":["sec13-F02","sec13-R14","sec13-F03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Look closely at how points get onto a record. The trigger is a conviction, not a traffic stop. Points are tied to convictions: the Department adds them once it is notified that you were convicted of a moving violation. The violation also has to have happened while your vehicle was moving. So the chain runs in order: a moving violation, a conviction, a notice to the Department, and then points added to your driving record. Each conviction adds to the total, and that total matters, because collecting too many points can cost you your driving privilege. The rest of this section explains how many points each violation brings and where the limits sit.","fact_ids":["sec13-F02","sec13-R14","sec13-F03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":45,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec13-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Points for speeding","fact_ids":["sec13-F04","sec13-F06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Points depend on the conviction.","fact_ids":["sec13-F04","sec13-F06"]},{"text":"Speeding example: two or three points by court level.","fact_ids":["sec13-F04","sec13-F06"]},{"text":"State law list: speeding is three points.","fact_ids":["sec13-F04","sec13-F06"]}],"narration":{"text":"How many points you get depends on the conviction. Speeding is the guide's example. A speeding conviction may bring two or three points, and the difference depends on whether the court that handled it was a municipal, county or state court. Later, the guide gives a list of state law violations with a point value for each one, and in that list speeding is worth three points. So the guide gives speeding a small range in its example and a single figure in its state list. Both are worth knowing, because a question can be written around either one, and the wording of the question tells you which of the two the writer had in mind.","fact_ids":["sec13-F04","sec13-F06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":46,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec13-u01-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Two or three, or three?","fact_ids":["sec13-R01","sec13-F04","sec13-F06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Example: two or three points, by court level.","fact_ids":["sec13-R01","sec13-F04","sec13-F06"]},{"text":"State law list: three points.","fact_ids":["sec13-R01","sec13-F04","sec13-F06"]},{"text":"Read which one the question means.","fact_ids":["sec13-R01","sec13-F04","sec13-F06"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap in this unit. Careless and imprudent driving and knowingly letting an unlicensed person drive carry the same value, four points each. Failing to stop for a loading or unloading school bus is five, not four. Driving with a suspended or revoked driver license is worth twelve points, so the second driver's conviction is worth far more. Failing to stop for a school bus that is loading or unloading students, five points. How long is her suspension?","fact_ids":["sec13-F14","sec13-F15"]},"answer":{"text":"Sixty days, because a second suspension for eight points in eighteen months lasts sixty days.","fact_ids":["sec13-F15"]},"rationale":{"text":"Point suspensions run thirty days the first time, sixty the second, and ninety the third or any later time.","fact_ids":["sec13-F15"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec13-u03-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"When points add up","fact_ids":["sec13-F13","sec13-F14","sec13-F16"]},"lines":[{"text":"Four in twelve months: an advisory.","fact_ids":["sec13-F13","sec13-F14","sec13-F16"]},{"text":"Eight or more in eighteen months: suspension.","fact_ids":["sec13-F13","sec13-F14","sec13-F16"]},{"text":"Higher totals: one-year revocation.","fact_ids":["sec13-F13","sec13-F14","sec13-F16"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson covers what happens as points add up. The guide sets three kinds of thresholds. The first is a warning: reaching a total of four points within twelve months gets you a point accumulation advisory from the Department. The second is a suspension: reaching eight or more points within eighteen months gets your driving privilege suspended. The third is a revocation for one year, which comes at three different combinations of points and months. Each threshold pairs a point total with a time window, so a question always needs both numbers. We will take the thresholds in order, then look at how long a suspension lasts and the pattern that links the revocation windows.","fact_ids":["sec13-F13","sec13-F14","sec13-F16"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":46,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec13-u03-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Advisory, then suspension","fact_ids":["sec13-F13","sec13-F14"]},"lines":[{"text":"Four points within twelve months: advisory.","fact_ids":["sec13-F13","sec13-F14"]},{"text":"Eight or more within eighteen months: suspended.","fact_ids":["sec13-F13","sec13-F14"]},{"text":"Both the points and the window change.","fact_ids":["sec13-F13","sec13-F14"]}],"narration":{"text":"Start with the two lower thresholds. Four points within twelve months brings a point accumulation advisory from the Department. That is a notice, not a loss of the privilege. The suspension threshold is higher and uses a longer window: reaching eight or more points within eighteen months gets your driving privilege suspended. Notice that both numbers change between the two thresholds. The points go from four to eight, and the window goes from twelve months to eighteen months. So a driver with four points in a year gets a letter, while a driver who reaches eight or more points within eighteen months loses the privilege for a time.","fact_ids":["sec13-F13","sec13-F14"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec13-u03-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"How long a suspension lasts","fact_ids":["sec13-F15","sec13-F14","sec13-R06"]},"lines":[{"text":"First time: thirty days.","fact_ids":["sec13-F15","sec13-F14","sec13-R06"]},{"text":"Second time: sixty days.","fact_ids":["sec13-F15","sec13-F14","sec13-R06"]},{"text":"Third or any later time: ninety days.","fact_ids":["sec13-F15","sec13-F14","sec13-R06"]}],"narration":{"text":"When the eight-point threshold is reached, the length of the suspension depends on how many times it has happened. A suspension for eight points in eighteen months lasts thirty days the first time. The second time, it lasts sixty days. The third time, and any later time, it lasts ninety days. So the lengths climb by thirty days for each of the first three suspensions and then stay at ninety. Keep this ladder of thirty, sixty and ninety days separate in your mind from the school bus suspensions you will meet later in this section, because those use different lengths. Here we are only talking about suspensions for points.","fact_ids":["sec13-F15","sec13-F14","sec13-R06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec13-u03-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Three revocation windows","fact_ids":["sec13-F16","sec13-R03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Twelve or more points in twelve months.","fact_ids":["sec13-F16","sec13-R03"]},{"text":"Eighteen or more in twenty-four months.","fact_ids":["sec13-F16","sec13-R03"]},{"text":"Twenty-four or more in thirty-six months.","fact_ids":["sec13-F16","sec13-R03"]},{"text":"Each step adds six points and twelve months.","fact_ids":["sec13-F16","sec13-R03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Revocation is the heaviest point action, and it lasts one year. Your driving privilege is revoked for one year if you reach twelve or more points in twelve months, eighteen or more in twenty-four months, or twenty-four or more in thirty-six months.
